items.summary: The Third Circuit affirmed James Bost's conviction for felon-in-possession of a firearm in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) in case No. 24-1719. Bost had been convicted in 2002 of terroristic threats and criminal conspiracy in a carjacking incident and was later found in possession of a stolen pistol. The court held that convictions for crimes demonstrating a prima facie risk of physical violence from firearm misuse support presumptive disarmament under the Second Amendment framework.

items.summary: The Third Circuit affirmed a district court judgment finding that 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1), as applied to Edward Williams, violates the Second Amendment. Williams had been convicted of two driving under the influence offenses, the second of which triggered the federal firearms prohibition for those convicted of crimes punishable by more than one year's imprisonment. The court held that regulations restricting firearm possession based on criminal convictions must target individuals who pose a risk of physical violence.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit affirmed the denial of qualified immunity to Officer Chance Avery in a Fourth Amendment excessive force case. Officer Avery fired three fatal shots at Christopher Poor approximately 16 seconds after Poor entered a residence holding a baseball bat down by his side and took one step in Avery's direction. The court held that Avery's use of deadly force was objectively unreasonable under Fourth Amendment law as clearly established at the time of the incident.

items.summary: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed Carlos Gutierrez-Hernandez's 56-month prison sentence for illegal reentry after prior deportation in case No. 26-10552. The district court calculated his guideline range as 46 to 57 months based on his base offense level, enhancements for repeat offense and prior burglary conviction, and a three-level reduction for acceptance of responsibility. items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit affirmed the dismissal of a habeas corpus petition filed by Dr. Rasha Alawieh, a Lebanese citizen with an H-1B visa, who challenged a Customs and Border Patrol expedited removal order and H-1B visa revocation. The court determined it lacked jurisdiction to review the expedited removal order and its consequences under statutory bars in the Immigration and Naturalization Act. Alawieh was issued the removal order on March 14, 2025, after CBP officers found images of Hassan Nasrallah and other content on her phone during secondary inspection at Boston Logan Airport.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit reversed in part a 180-month sentence for fentanyl possession with intent to distribute, holding that the district court erred in applying a two-level stash-house enhancement. The court found that Conill-Perez's possession of a hotel room for several hours did not constitute 'maintenance' of the premises as required by the sentencing guidelines, noting the absence of evidence that he entered or exited the room or exercised control over it. The court affirmed the criminal-history assessment and remanded the case for resentencing.

items.opening_verbatim:
United States Court of Appeals
For the Seventh Circuit
Chicago, Illinois 60604

Submitted October 13, 2026
Decided October 13, 2026

Before

FRANK H. EASTERBROOK, Circuit Judge

THOMAS L. KIRSCH II, Circuit Judge

JOSHUA P. KOLAR, Circuit J
items.summary: Eugene Alexander was convicted by jury of possessing over 500 grams of cocaine with intent to distribute and sentenced to 180 months' imprisonment. His appointed counsel filed an Anders brief asserting the appeal was frivolous, and the Court of Appeals found no merit to challenge the denial of his motion to suppress evidence, the sufficiency of evidence, or his joint trial with a codefendant. The court affirmed the conviction.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-11807; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00220-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.A. Helicopters AGENCY: Federal Aviation Admin
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-18-01, which applies to Leonardo S.p.A. Model A119 and AW119 MKII helicopters. AD 2024-18-01 requires repetitive inspections of certain collective stick torque tube assemblies for deficiencies and corrective action, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-18-01, an improved collective stick torque tube assembly was designed, and replacement instructions were issued. This proposed AD would require repetitive inspections of certain collective stick torque tube assemblies and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacement of affected parts. This proposed AD would also require modification of the helicopter through replacement of an affected part with a serviceable part, which would constitute terminating action for the repetitive inspections. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of an affected part on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this airworthiness directive (AD) to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.A. Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY 8 CFR Part 214 [CIS No. 2870-26; DHS Docket No. USCIS-2026-0529] RIN 1615-AD26 Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility AGENCY: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, DHS. ACTION: N
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), proposes to remove 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which generally provides that USCIS gives deference to a prior approval involving the same facts when adjudicating a request to extend a petition for an alien's employment or stay. This change would better align DHS regulations with the statute, which places the burden of proving eligibility for all immigration benefits on the petitioner, applicant, or beneficiary; strengthen adjudicatory review; and support agency priorities to improve the integrity of the immigration system and better protect the interests of U.S. workers.
items.title: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE Drug Enforcement Administration 21 CFR Part 1308 [Docket No. DEA-1644] Schedules of Controlled Substances: Temporary Placement of MGM-15 and MGM-16 in Schedule I AGENCY: Drug Enforcement Administration, Department of J
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is issuing this notice of intent to publish a temporary order to schedule two 7-hydroxymitragynine-related substances (MGM-15 and MGM-16), including their isomers, esters, ethers, salts, and salts of isomers, esters, and ethers, whenever the existence of such isomers, esters, ethers, and salts is possible, in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). On August 26, 2026, DEA published a temporary order placing mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, MGM-15, and MGM-16 in schedule I of the CSA. Today, DEA is providing notice of its intent to publish a new temporary order for MGM-15 and MGM-16 that will maintain the temporary placement of these substances in schedule I of the CSA without change. Separately in this Federal Register , DEA is publishing a notice of intent relating to mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, in response to a letter sent by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) dated October 6, 2026. HHS's letter related only to mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. Therefore, DEA is publishing this notice of intent only for the technical and procedural purpose of distinguishing MGM-15 and MGM-16 from mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. [official summary truncated; see source]
items.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Temporary Placement of MGM-15 and MGM-16 in Schedule I

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE Drug Enforcement Administration 21 CFR Part 1308 [Docket No. DEA-1570] Schedules of Controlled Substances: Temporary Placement of 7- Hydroxymitragynine and Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl Above a Specified Threshold in Sched
items.summary: The Administrator of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is issuing this notice of intent to publish a temporary order to schedule 7-hydroxymitragynine and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (including their isomers, esters, ethers, salts, and salts of isomers, esters, and ethers, whenever the existence of such isomers, esters, ethers, and salts is possible) when either substance alone, or their combined amount if both are present, is above a specified threshold, in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Based on a different threshold provided by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in July of 2025, DEA published a notice of intent to temporarily schedule 7-hydroxymitragynine above that lower threshold on July 7, 2026. Additionally, DEA published a temporary order placing mitragynine pseudoindoxyl without a threshold in schedule I of the CSA on August 26, 2026. On October 8, 2026, HHS sent a letter recommending that DEA place of the CSA 7-hydroxymitragynine and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl in schedule I when either substance alone, or their combined amount if both are present, is above a new specified threshold. [official summary truncated; see source]
items.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Temporary Placement of 7- Hydroxymitragynine and Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl Above a Specified Threshold in Schedule I

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY 8 CFR Part 274a [CIS No. 2859-26; DHS Docket No. USCIS-2025-0271] RIN 1615-AD05 Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents AGENCY: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
items.summary: On October 30, 2025, DHS published an interim final rule (IFR) that amended DHS regulations to end the practice of automatically extending the validity of employment authorization documents (Forms I-766 or EADs) for aliens who have timely filed an application to renew their EAD in certain employment authorization categories. This final rule responds to comments received on the IFR and reaffirms and finalizes the provisions of the IFR. Ending the automatic extension of EADs enhances benefit integrity and prioritizes the proper vetting and screening of aliens before granting a new period of employment authorization and/or a new EAD.
items.title: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY 8 CFR Part 207 [CIS No. 2856-26; DHS Docket No. USCIS-2026-0397] RIN 1615-AD23 Removing 30-Day Refugee Termination Notice AGENCY: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Department of Homeland Security (DH
items.summary: This interim final rule (IFR) amends Department of Homeland Security (DHS) regulations to expedite termination of refugee status when DHS determines an alien was not a refugee within the meaning of section 101(a)(42) of the Immigration and Nationality Act at the time of admission to the United States. The response period to a Notice of Intent to Terminate (NOIT) is reduced from thirty to ten days. These changes aim to restore integrity to the immigration system, mitigate risks to national security and public safety, and prevent fraud and exploitation.
items.title: Removing 30-Day Refugee Termination Notice

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Baykar Piaggio Aerospace S.p.A. (Piaggio) Model P-180 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of corrosion and cracks found around the head of attaching fasteners on main wing lower skin external reinforcement doublers. This proposed AD would require repetitive high frequency eddy current (HFEC) inspections of the lower skin reinforcement and, depending on findings, corrective action. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Baykar Piaggio Aerospace S.p.A. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Piaggio Aviation S.p.A.) Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2025-0204; Project Identifier AD-2024-00327-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Adminis
items.summary: The FAA is withdrawing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) that proposed to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) that would have applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. The NPRM was prompted by reports that very high frequency (VHF) radio frequencies transfer between the active and standby windows of the tuning control panel (TCP) without flightcrew input. The uncommanded frequency changes could result in missed communications between the flightcrew and Air Traffic Control. The NPRM would have required updating the TCP operational software (OPS) and performing a software configuration check. Since issuance of the NPRM, the FAA has determined that the TCP OPS version specified in the NPRM does not correct the unsafe condition. Accordingly, the NPRM is withdrawn.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-2289; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01592-T; Amendment 39-23482; AD 2026-20-09] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airpla
items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model BD-700-2A12 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of low clearance in the right wing between the fuel line flexible coupling and the harness support bracket clip-nut, between the fuel line flexible coupling and hydraulic system, and between the hydraulic system and fuel vent tube. This AD requires rectifying the low clearance condition between the fuel line flexible coupling and the harness support bracket clip-nut, rectifying the low clearance condition between the fuel line flexible coupling and the hydraulic system, and doing an inspection for adequate clearance between the hydraulic system and the fuel vent tube and applicable on-conditions actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-05-06, which applies to all Leonardo S.p.a Model AW169 helicopters. items.summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is amending its regulations to renew the AP1000 design certification and incorporate Revision 20 of the AP1000 design control document. The purpose of this rulemaking action is to update the AP1000 design to be consistent with changes made to the design during the licensing, construction, and operation of Vogtle Electric Generating Plant, Units 3 and 4. This rulemaking incorporates AP1000 design control document Revision 20, which includes updates made to the AP1000 design to represent a current, construction-validated design. The NRC is also issuing an environmental assessment supporting this rule.

items.summary: The Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act of 2026, introduced in September 2026 and reported with amendment in October 2026, requires the Small Business Administration Administrator to develop and disseminate cybersecurity information and resources to small businesses in consultation with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and National Institute of Standards and Technology. The bill mandates the SBA provide information to small businesses seeking federal contracts regarding the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification program and directs the Administrator to consult annually on best practices for disseminating cybersecurity information. The Administrator must submit annual reports to Congress describing the number and details of small businesses that contacted the agency regarding cybersecurity matters.
